<STRUCT_0001>
A separation condition on an algebraic space <MATH_0001> is a condition
on the diagonal morphism <MATH_0002>. Let us first
list the properties the diagonal has automatically.
Since the diagonal is representable by definition the following lemma
makes sense (through
Definition <REF_0001>).

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme contained in <MATH_0002>.
Let <MATH_0003> be an algebraic space over <MATH_0004>.
Let <MATH_0005> be the diagonal morphism.
Then
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0006> is locally of finite type,
<STRUCT_0003> <MATH_0007> is a monomorphism,
<STRUCT_0004> <MATH_0008> is separated, and
<STRUCT_0005> <MATH_0009> is locally quasi-finite.
<STRUCT_0006>

Let <MATH_0001> be a presentation of <MATH_0002>.
As in the proof of Lemma <REF_0001> the diagram
<MATH_0003>
is cartesian. Hence according to
Lemma <REF_0002>
it suffices to show that <MATH_0004> has the properties listed in the lemma.
(Note that each of the properties (1) -- (4) occur in the lists
of Remarks <REF_0003>
and <REF_0004>.)
Since <MATH_0005> is an equivalence relation it is a monomorphism.
Hence it is separated by
Schemes, Lemma <REF_0005>.
As <MATH_0006> is an <ACCENT_0001>tale equivalence relation we see that
<MATH_0007> are <ACCENT_0002>tale. Hence <MATH_0008> are locally of finite
type. Then it follows from
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0006> that
<MATH_0009> is locally of finite type. Finally, as it is a monomorphism
its fibres are finite. Thus we conclude that it is locally quasi-finite by
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0007>.
